budget.reason: ours, written 2026-11-20 before the first VM run; the test plan names no number. 900 s is the runbook's own budget for empty directory -> TD_MEC_DEV_01 passed with the environments already installed (33 s measured on this PC on 2026-11-18); the other 900 s are for what a clean VM adds: boot and cloud-init, fetching the code, and the install blocks downloading the CSE, the test runner and their dependencies from PyPI. Half an hour is one sitting for a developer onboarding.

ipv6_closed.setting: ipv6=off in the netdev line (QEMU's option that turns IPv6 off; libslirp's in6_enabled=0)
ipv6_closed.unreachable_over_ipv6: everything: libslirp drops every IPv6 frame the VM sends and answers none (no router advertisement, neighbour, DHCPv6 or DNS answer), so over IPv6 the VM reaches neither this host ([::1], ::ffff:127.0.0.1) nor the LAN nor the IPv6 internet, on any port
ipv6_closed.reachable_over_ipv4: only the two guestfwd targets 10.0.2.100:8080 and 10.0.2.101:3128 (restrict=on: the host alias 10.0.2.2 gets a reset, UDP is not delivered)
ipv6_closed.how_shown: 2026-11-20, before any VM run: this host's libslirp 4.9.5 loaded in-process (no QEMU), configured from the harness's netdev value (restricted=1, in6_enabled=0) with a guestfwd exec rule at 10.0.2.100; the second check's frames were fed to it unchanged: an IPv6 SYN to fec0::2 from the crafted source fec0:0:a00:264::1234, an IPv6 SYN to ::ffff:127.0.0.1, an IPv6 SYN from an ordinary source, IPv6 and IPv4 UDP. None opened a connection on this host and no IPv6 frame drew any frame back. Control: the netdev value before ipv6=off (in6_enabled=1) with the same frames opened host connections to [::1] and 127.0.0.1. After the guest's ARP, an IPv4 SYN to 10.0.2.100 still drew slirp's SYN-ACK and one to 10.0.2.2 a reset, in both configurations
ipv6_closed.not_shown: QEMU itself was not run (not installed on this host when this was written): that -netdev ipv6=off reaches libslirp as in6_enabled=0 is taken from QEMU's documentation of the option, not observed here; in the run the VM's own IPv6 addresses are read, and one other than loopback or link-local is an integrity problem

network.statement: restrict=on and ipv6=off: over IPv4 the VM reaches nothing on this host, its LAN or the internet except the two guestfwd targets; over IPv6 it reaches nothing at all; slirp's restricted mode gives it no DNS; no port of this host is forwarded into the VM

rerun_block.text:
: runbook-step rerun phase=rerun && \
cd "$ROOT" && "$PY" -B estimed/clean_rerun.py rerun --reference /home/edgefollow/vm-harness/reference.json

runbook.rerun_cwd: edgefollow's home; the block runs exactly as written (the harness adds no cd)
runbook.root: only the install blocks marked root=yes ran as root (the root step, started by run.sh); every other runbook block ran as edgefollow, who has no sudo

steps.create-user: cloud-init creates user edgefollow: password locked (none is set), no SSH key, no sudo and no admin group; no other user is created
steps.no-ssh-keys: cloud-init: password login off, root login off, the image's host keys deleted and none generated
steps.power-off: cloud-init power_state: power off once the harness script has ended
steps.progress: a progress line on the serial console
steps.probe-root: read-only facts as root: edgefollow's password state and groups, the files in /etc/ssh, edgefollow's home before delivery
steps.fetch: curl: code.tar, guest.py (this file) and reference.json from the host's seed server at 10.0.2.100:8080 (a guestfwd target)
steps.check: sha256sum --check of the three fetched files against the SHA-256s written in user-data
steps.root-blocks: as root (run.sh runs as root): vm_rerun.py root -- RUNBOOK.md and clean_rerun.py read from the checked code.tar into a folder of root's; ONLY the install blocks marked root=yes, in the runbook's order, each exactly as written through clean_rerun's Executor (bash -c, from /root), with exactly the environment PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin HOME=/root LANG=C.UTF-8, every name the runbook's variables block exports, HTTPS_PROXY and https_proxy (step proxy) and APT_CONFIG (step apt-proxy); their ids, SHA-256s and exit codes go to the serial console from root itself and to root_blocks.json. No other block is run as root
steps.deliver: as edgefollow: make ROOT (the runbook's variables-block value) and the harness folder, unpack code.tar into ROOT, copy the harness files (the guest reads the root step's root_blocks.json where root wrote it, mode 0644)
steps.guest: as edgefollow: vm_rerun.py guest -- facts read in-process, then the install blocks NOT marked root=yes and then the runbook's rerun block, each exactly as written through clean_rerun's Executor (bash -c, from edgefollow's home: the harness adds no cd; a cd inside a block runs), with exactly the environment PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/home/edgefollow LANG=C.UTF-8 and every name the runbook's variables block exports (the install blocks also HTTPS_PROXY and https_proxy, step proxy); then the uploads. The guest driver itself starts with HOME USER LOGNAME PATH LANG only
steps.proxy: every install block's environment (root=yes or not), and nothing else's, gets HTTPS_PROXY and https_proxy = http://10.0.2.101:3128, this host's allow-listing CONNECT proxy: with restrict=on and ipv6=off the VM has no other way out. No runbook command is changed; the rerun block runs without it
steps.apt-proxy: the root blocks' environment, and nothing else's, gets APT_CONFIG=/var/lib/vmrerun/apt-proxy.conf, a file the root step writes: Acquire::http::Proxy and Acquire::https::Proxy = http://10.0.2.101:3128. apt reaches the image's https://deb.debian.org sources through CONNECT deb.debian.org:443
steps.network: QEMU user-mode networking with restrict=on, ipv6=off and exactly two guestfwd rules (the seed server and the proxy, each through a relay to one port on this host's 127.0.0.1); no port forward into the VM
steps.summary: the guest's summary as one line on the serial console

does_not_show: one VM type: QEMU with KVM on this PC (i7-6700HQ), 2 vCPUs, 4 GB, an 8 GB overlay disk, user-mode networking with restrict=on
one base image: the Debian 13 genericcloud amd64 cloud image; no other distribution or image was tried
Debian's SHA512SUMS is not signature-checked: the image is compared with the SHA512SUMS file downloaded next to it from the same server; its OpenPGP signature (SHA512SUMS.sign) was not verified
pip pulls the dependencies of the pinned packages unpinned from PyPI during the run; another day can resolve other versions, and a PyPI or network outage would fail the install blocks
a script followed the runbook, not a human: it ran the blocks exactly as written and cannot misread the prose around them, so text a person would trip over is not tested
the original execution (the reference) was made on this host from the working tree of 2026-11-18; the VM ran HEAD (see code.vs_reference_commit for the files that differ)

the VM reached only the seed server and the allow-listing proxy (pypi.org:443, files.pythonhosted.org:443, deb.debian.org:443), both on this host through guestfwd over IPv4; it had no DNS (slirp's restricted mode drops it), so the proxy resolved names here and refused non-public addresses. A developer's VM with a full internet connection has none of these limits: a block that fetches from another host fails here

IPv6 was off (ipv6=off): restrict=on alone let a crafted IPv6 SYN open host connections in libslirp 4.9.5. That ipv6=off closes it was shown with this host's libslirp run in-process (in6_enabled=0, the value QEMU's ipv6=off sets), not with QEMU, which was not installed when the harness was written; the VM's own list of IPv6 addresses is read in the run and an address other than loopback or link-local is an integrity problem

apt is given the proxy only in the root-marked install blocks, through APT_CONFIG; the image's apt sources are https://deb.debian.org (read from the image), so apt uses CONNECT deb.debian.org:443. apt over http:// would get 405 from this CONNECT-only proxy, and a mirror other than deb.debian.org would get 403

unattended-upgrades and systemd-timesyncd are not disabled by any harness step: with restrict=on, ipv6=off and APT_CONFIG set only in the root blocks' environment neither can fetch or sync from the network, but they may still run and take CPU or the dpkg lock; the runbook's root block waits for the dpkg lock (DPkg::Lock::Timeout), and whether apt-get update also waits for the package-list lock with that option was not checked here

the whole in-VM evidence chain but the root blocks' console line (the guest driver, clean_rerun.py, the uploads, summary.json) runs as edgefollow, the same user as the code under test: a program that lies could forge a consistent PASS inside the VM. This host checks what it can (hashes of the delivered code and runbook, the executed-command log against the delivered runbook, its own clock), not the honesty of what ran in the VM

the VM's clock is used for no verdict: step 5's time is an upper bound, from QEMU's start to this host's receipt of the VM's clean_rerun record, so it also holds clean_rerun's shutdown and controls after TD_MEC_DEV_01

the base image was copied, and hashed while copying, into a 0700 folder of this user on a local filesystem and re-hashed after the run; a process of this same user could change and restore the copy during the run, which the re-hash after it cannot see

the rerun block ran from edgefollow's home directory, exactly as written: the harness adds no cd, and a cd inside the block runs. clean_rerun.py reads no phase=rerun block (its parser refuses any phase but variables, install, bootstrap, test and shutdown in a shell fence), so the block sits in a fence clean_rerun.py skips and the harness alone recognises it, with clean_rerun's marker and && rules
clean_rerun.py's own two NOT-RUN rows are fixed text written for this PC; inside the VM both are covered by this record (the VM is fresh, and the install blocks were run)
